header:
Drexel University
United States · Mathematics PhD
Roster and rank verification handled separately
Eligibility and preparation · Deadlines by stage · English and GRE · Academic records · Recommendation letters · Written
materials · Funding and fees · Conflicts and remaining checks · Faculty · Sources
Pay attention to
• December 1 is the current final PhD deadline; do not rely on the older January 15 factsheet.
• Official transcripts are required for review, unlike many programs accepting unofficial uploads.
• The mathematics English waiver and GRE policies need direct clarification.

sections.title: Eligibility and preparation
sections.text:
Eligibility for your route [Standing rule]
A four-year US accredited bachelor’s degree qualifies for consideration; regular admission typically requires
undergraduate GPA 3.0 and any graduate GPA at least 3.0. Mathematics PhD is full-time. International
applicants are eligible; completion of UChicago degree remains necessary. [s1] [s3]
Before submission [Standing rule]
Choose one program only; arrange official transcripts directly from every institution and three referees early.
Check English waiver with enroll@drexel.edu. Submit the application, essay and résumé, then monitor
Discover Drexel. Mailed records can take 3-4 weeks to process. [s1] [s2]
Adviser contact [Standing rule]
Current research fit is clearest in algebraic combinatorics and noncommutative/complex analysis. No prior
supervisor commitment is listed. Contact prospective faculty about supervision; number theory in broad
marketing does not by itself establish an available adviser. [s1] [s7]
Portal workflow [Standing rule]
After processing, admissions emails a Student ID and PIN for Discover Drexel status access; a separate email
confirms the entire file is complete. Individual letter-receipt display details are not specified. [s2]
Cycle verification [Standing rule]
Standing admissions checklist; no explicit Fall 2027 confirmation of December 1 or stipend. [s1]

sections.title: English and GRE
sections.text:
English requirement [Standing rule]
Mathematics publishes TOEFL iBT 100 (older scale; paper 600/computer 250), IELTS 7.0, PTE 68 or Duolingo
110 unless waived. New 2026 TOEFL scale threshold is not published here. Official scores use school code
2194, no department code. [s1] [s2]
UChicago English exemption [Unresolved]
The mathematics page allows waivers but does not state the qualifying US-degree rule or whether an
unfinished degree qualifies. Engineering, online and business pages have differing scope; their exemptions
were not transferred to mathematics. Obtain a written ruling from enroll@drexel.edu for your UChicago
degree. [s1] [s3]
GRE General; GRE Mathematics [Unresolved]
Neither GRE General nor Mathematics is listed in the current program checklist. Central instructions say
requirements vary and some programs consider voluntary scores for admissions/fellowships. This silence does
not establish whether mathematics scores are optional, discouraged or not considered; confirm both tests with
the program. [s1] [s2]

sections.title: Academic records
sections.text:
Transcripts and degree records [Standing rule]
Official transcripts must come directly from every attended college/university even if credits transferred.
Include course grades and degree conferrals; submit degree certificates when conferral is absent. Non-English
records need original language plus exact institutional or ATA-certified translation. Single-lifetime transcripts
require course-by-course evaluation; admissions may request evaluation of international records at applicant
expense. Already-graduated international applicants email certificates as PDF or Word to enroll@drexel.edu.
[s1]
Mathematics-course list; Course descriptions [Standing rule]
Not listed as a separate required item on the public mathematics application checklist. This does not establish
whether the current portal permits an optional upload; exact prompt, length, formatting and upload/link rule
are not published. [s1]

sections.title: Recommendation letters
sections.text:
Number and type [Standing rule]
Three letters; electronic requests through application or Discover Drexel. Alternatively, unopened mailed
envelopes with recommender address, telephone and signature are accepted. [s1]
Scholarship references [Unresolved]
No separate mathematics assistantship application or extra scholarship reference is listed. Central instructions
direct applicants to financial-assistance information; named fellowship-specific essays, references and
deadlines remain unverified. [s1] [s2]
What sends the invitation; Before versus after submission [Standing rule]
The applicant enters referee names/contact details and can request recommendations in the application or
after submission through Discover Drexel. The public wording does not identify whether merely saving contact
information sends email or a separate send action is necessary. [s1]
Receipt confirmation [Standing rule]
After processing, admissions emails a Student ID and PIN for Discover Drexel status access; a separate email
confirms the entire file is complete. Individual letter-receipt display details are not specified. [s2]

Updating and reusing letters [Unresolved]
Not established by the cited public admissions materials. Confirm in the current application or with graduate
admissions before relying on a rule.

sections.text:
Academic CV / resume [Standing rule]
Required résumé; upload in application or Discover Drexel after submission. No length or formatting limit is
published. [s1]
Statement of purpose; Personal / background statement [Standing rule]
Required essay, approximately 500 words. Faithful prompt paraphrase: explain why Drexel, near- and
long-term career plans, and how your background, experience, interests or values together with this degree
support those goals. Upload with application or through Discover Drexel afterward; font, spacing and file-type
limits are not public. This is one essay, not two separate statements. [s1]

sections.title: Funding and fees
sections.text:
Amount and coverage [Unresolved]
Assistantships provide stipend, full tuition and a health-insurance subsidy. No verified mathematics annual
stipend, paid-month count or summer guarantee was found; university says stipend varies by program. Obtain
a 2027 offer breakdown. [s4] [s5]
Years of support [Standing rule]
Department describes assistantship support for up to five years; older factsheet describes five years for
students making satisfactory progress. Exact renewal, summer and health terms belong in the offer. [s4] [s6]
International eligibility [Standing rule]
University assistantships are available to US and non-US citizens enrolled full-time. [s5]
Conditions and duties [Standing rule]
Assistantships require teaching or research service and satisfactory progress; department targets five-year
PhD completion. [s4] [s5]
Extra funding application [Unresolved]
No separate mathematics assistantship application or extra scholarship reference is listed. Central instructions
direct applicants to financial-assistance information; named fellowship-specific essays, references and
deadlines remain unverified. [s1] [s2]
Other funding routes [Standing rule]
Teaching and research assistantships are identified; central instructions also mention scholarship/fellowship
review and possible use of GRE scores. International eligibility and application rules for individual named
awards require confirmation. [s2] [s5]
Application fee [Standing rule]
US $65 application fee. [s1]

Fee waiver [Unresolved]
No mathematics-specific fee-waiver procedure or international eligibility rule was found in the checked
mathematics and central application pages. Ask enroll@drexel.edu before paying. [s1] [s2]
